The big picture

What is Hive?

Think of Hive as one shared network that many different apps run on — all using the same account that you control.

One account

A single Hive account works everywhere — no new sign-up for every app.

One ecosystem

Social, games, communities, and apps all share the same network and account.

You control it

Your keys, your account. You decide what gets signed and what doesn't.

Hive AccountSocialGamesCommunitiesdAppsKeychain
Your account

Your Hive account, and its keys

Hive accounts use different keys for different permissions — so a key for posting can't move your funds, and vice versa.

Social

Posting Key

Used for everyday social actions — posting, commenting, and voting. The key you'll use most often.

Financial

Active Key

Used for transfers, managing assets, and governance. Anything that moves value or changes your account.

Messaging

Memo Key

Used to encrypt and decrypt private memos attached to transfers, so notes stay confidential.

Master

Owner Key

The most powerful key. It can recover your account and regenerate every other key. Keep it offline.

Your keys are your responsibility.

Keep backups of your keys stored safely offline, and never paste a private key into a website. Keychain keeps your Active, Posting, and Memo keys on your device — your Owner key should stay offline.

The tokens

HIVE, Hive Power & HBD

Three forms of value on Hive. Here's how they relate to each other — in plain terms.

HIVE

The main token of the Hive blockchain. Liquid and transferable — used for transactions, trades, and powering up.

Hive Power HP

HIVE in its vested form. More Hive Power means more voting weight, more resource credits, and more governance influence.

HBD

A stablecoin pegged to the US dollar. Used for stable-value transactions, and can be locked in savings to earn interest.

Power UpHIVE→Hive Power

Convert liquid HIVE into Hive Power to gain influence and resources.

Stable valueHIVE↔HBD

Move between HIVE and HBD — a dollar-pegged stablecoin for steady value.

Security

Stay safe

Three rules that keep your account secure. That's it — keep these in mind and you're most of the way there.

1

Never share your private keys

No legitimate app or person will ever ask for your private keys. Keep them to yourself.

2

Check what you're approving

Read the request before you tap Approve. Understand what action Keychain is about to sign.

3

Keep your keys backed up

Store your keys safely offline. A secure backup is how you recover access if you ever need to.

A website asks you to paste your Active Key?

Don't do it. Use Keychain to approve the action instead — your key never leaves your device.
